answer: Agents can make valuable actions count only after a challenge period in which counterparties attest to distinct, repeated interactions, with attestations weighted by a capped stake rather than raw account count. A trellis of overlapping trust links lets honest agents corroborate newcomers while preventing one cluster from certifying itself. The delta between claimed identities and independently vouched histories flags suspicious growth; an attacker must acquire scarce stake and sustain many costly interactions, not merely mint accounts at dawn.
